question: \(X,\) \(Y,\) and \(Z\) are pairwise disjoint sets of people. The average ages of people in the sets \(X,\) \(Y,\) \(Z,\) \(X\cup Y,\) \(X\cup Z,\) and \(Y\cup Z\) are given in the table below. \[\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline \text{Set} & X & Y & Z & X\cup Y & X\cup Z & Y\cup Z\\ \hline \text{Average age of people in the set} & 37 & 23 & 41 & 29 & 39.5 & 33\\ \hline\end{array}\] Find the average age of the people in the set \(X\cup Y\cup Z.\)
solution:
A combined average is weighted by the numbers of people in the groups. The pairwise averages therefore let us recover the relative group sizes.

Let \(x,y,z\) be the numbers of people in \(X,Y,Z\), respectively. They are positive because each group has a stated average. Since the sets are disjoint, the total age in \(X\cup Y\) is \(37x+23y\), and its population is \(x+y\). Thus
\[
37x+23y=29(x+y),
\]
which simplifies to \(8x=6y\). Therefore \(x:y=3:4\).

Similarly, the average for \(X\cup Z\) gives
\[
37x+41z=39.5(x+z),
\]
so \(2.5x=1.5z\), giving \(x:z=3:5\). Together these imply
\[
x:y:z=3:4:5.
\]
These weights also reproduce the remaining pairwise average:
\[
\frac{4\cdot23+5\cdot41}{4+5}=\frac{297}{9}=33.
\]
The common scale of the populations cancels when we compute the overall average. Consequently, the average age in the union of all three groups is
\[
\frac{3\cdot37+4\cdot23+5\cdot41}{3+4+5}
=\frac{408}{12}
=\boxed{34}\text{ years},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
